Adolion: The Eastern Road
Author view
Overview
Memory
⚑
Where you are
The Final Before the Emperor
At the tournament arena.
Under a golden canopy the Emperor takes his seat and the herald calls the champion against your group. What you do with what you know is up to you.
What happens next is yours to decide.
The scene is tense.
About this story
You are a C-rank party from the Aegis City Adventurers Guild, weeks out across the Jehopa Ocean, coming ashore at Hianxo, capital of the Third Kingdom, with an invitation to fight in the Jiansho Tournament and a kitsune guide waiting on the dock. Expect duels in a packed arena, court manners with knives behind them, and whatever the road inland holds once the tournament is done. Play the party's leader, travelling with Belle and Dalan.
Recently
You left The Night Before the Final behind and moved into The Final Before the Emperor.
Open threads
Megumi's intent in the register and her fixation on Honami remain unexplained as the final approaches.
Honami's pride and worry over the party reaching the final hint at stakes she has not disclosed.
The party must decide how to counter the poisoned ward-post thread before the final, since striking the opposing fighter could trigger the venom and frame them.
Whoever strung the poisoned thread between the ward-posts — and their link to Megumi's register notes — remains unidentified.
The party must win the final against Talxo Xianxu without landing a strike that triggers the poisoned thread, or disarm it first.
The story so far
The party crossed the Jehopa Ocean and arrived in Hianxo, a city of red lacquer and cedar roofs, seeking group entry into the tournament at Jiansho Academy. At the harbour they were greeted by Honami, a three-tailed woman, who led them up the hill with Dalan following nervously. At the Academy, Megumi Xianxu welcomed Belle and Max Nightriver as Honami's guests and read the tournament rules aloud: bouts ended in submission, knockout, or ring-out; death was regretted but not punished; and the final would be fought before the Emperor himself for a prize from his hand.
